headline: Browne's five-touchdown night powers Michigan past UCLA 51-28
dek: Both teams even their records at 1-1 and climb to sixth in the power poll with division implications looming.
body: The game's final statement arrived with 27 seconds left in the fourth quarter when Tommie Browne handed to Eric Brock at the 50 and the back burst 42 yards for a touchdown that made it 51-28, capping a three-play, 50-yard drive that took just 26 seconds.

Michigan struck first on the opening drive when Calvin Wendtland raced 29 yards for a score at 13:02 of the first quarter, and the Wolverines never trailed; UCLA answered with a 13-yard Nico Iamaleava-to-Marcus Harris strike to tie it at 7, but Michigan reeled off 20 straight points — a Vince Burkett plunge, a 25-yard Browne-to-Steve Gardner connection, and a Brock one-yard run — to lead 27-7 at halftime; the Bruins cut it to 27-14 on a Kenneth Moore III five-yard catch early in the third, yet a Herbie Swanson field goal and a Wendtland three-yard touchdown after a UCLA fumble pushed the margin to 37-14; Leland Smith caught two late Iamaleava touchdowns sandwiched around a Browne-to-Jakob Salas four-yard score before Brock's closing dash sealed the 23-point final margin.

The box score shows mirror-image first-down totals at 28 apiece and nearly identical yardage — Michigan 519, UCLA 479 — but the difference lived in the ground game and ball security: Michigan rushed for 183 yards and two Brock touchdowns against 111 for UCLA, converted 67 percent of third downs to UCLA's 63 percent, and committed zero turnovers while the Bruins lost two fumbles, one by Jalen Berger in the second quarter and one by Iamaleava in the third that set up a short Michigan touchdown drive; Iamaleava still threw for 368 yards and four scores, lifting his season total to 646 yards and 10 touchdowns with zero interceptions and a 138.5 rating that ranks fourth in the PCFL, while Browne added 336 yards and two passing scores plus two rushing touchdowns from his backs to reach 467 yards and a 98.5 rating on the year.

Both squads move to 1-1 and rise from tenth to sixth in the power poll; UCLA sits third in the Western Pacific behind division leader USC with a loss on its streak, while Michigan claims the Western Central lead at 1-1 with a win streak of one; the Bruins host unbeaten Texas next week and the Wolverines welcome unbeaten LSU, matchups that will test whether either defense — UCLA allowing 405.5 yards per game and Michigan 467 — can slow the league's top offenses.
turningPoint: UCLA's fumble at its own 26-yard line early in the fourth quarter (Q4 14:21) gave Michigan a short field that Wendtland converted for a 37-14 lead, effectively putting the game out of reach.
byTheNumbers: Turnover margin: Michigan 0, UCLA 2 lost fumbles — the Bruins' two giveaways directly preceded 10 Michigan points and swung field position decisively.
Rushing advantage: Michigan 183 yards to UCLA 111, with Eric Brock's 80 yards and two scores providing a dimension the Bruins could not match.

Third-down efficiency: Michigan 6-of-9 (67%) versus UCLA 5-of-8 (63%) — the Wolverines sustained drives while the Bruins stalled on key possessions, including a fourth-down stop at the Michigan 42 in the third quarter.

Quarterback season arcs: Iamaleava's 10 touchdown passes rank fourth in the PCFL; Browne's 467 passing yards rank ninth, but his offense's balance produced 51 points against a defense allowing 36 per game entering the night.

unsungHero.name: Eric Brock
unsungHero.why: Rushed for 80 yards and two touchdowns on just eight carries, including the decisive 42-yard scoring run in the final minute that turned a comfortable lead into a rout.
